translation: There is again a [kind of] instance: while taking advantage of great heat of the weather, [a person] suffers it from toil on the road, or suffers it from taxing his form in the fields; or again one with a weak thin body who, eating little [and] toiling excessively; there are also those people of constant fasting who cultivate goodness, whose stomach qi has long been vacuous, and who suffer it from toil. All these are similar to the yangming heat-injury Bai Hu Tang pattern. There must be great heat when the body is felt; there must be restless heat, oppression and chaos; great aversion to heat, thirst, and drinking water. Because of the excessiveness of the toil, there is also pain of the body. At the time of first receiving the disease, [it] is especially similar to the external contraction of heat that is an excess pattern. If one wrongly administers Bai Hu Tang, death in ten days is certain. In this pattern the spleen and stomach are greatly vacuous and the Original Qi is insufficient; in both mouth and nose the qi is short and hurried and wheezes above. After the sun turns [midday], which is the time when the yangming gains its season, the disease must lessen somewhat. If it were an externally contracted heat disease, then at the time of the sun declining toward dusk [shen time] it must make great delerium, its heat increasing, with great thirst and drinking of water, vexation and oppression unceasing. Those with insufficiency from toil all do not have this pattern, and it is especially easy to decompose. If there is a pattern hard to settle and suspected [between the two], one must wait one or two days to seek the physician's treatment, and one will not make an error.
